verdict: Trainual: Choose Trainual when documenting SOPs and running employee training paths is the primary job — and you can work through demo/quote pricing. Scores use the HR editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing.
strengths: Strong SOP knowledge-base and training-path focus
weaknesses: No public seat dollars — demo/quote only
Value score hurt by pricing opacity
AI and SSO are higher-plan gated
bestFor: Growing companies (roughly 25–1000 employees) documenting SOPs and role training
Ops leaders who need searchable playbooks with completion tracking
Teams that can engage sales for demos and accept implementation onboarding
notIdealFor: Micro teams that need transparent self-serve seat pricing
Buyers whose primary job is ATS hiring or GPS time clocks
Course creators selling public LMS commerce (LearnWorlds)
tradeoffs: Published free tiers vs paid depth for ATS, WFM, time, or training jobs
Hub / multi-module pricing complexity vs single-product floors
Mobile/frontline readiness vs desk-bound admin depth
Opaque contact-sales pricing vs transparent published seats
recommendation: Choose Trainual when documenting SOPs and running employee training paths is the primary job — and you can work through demo/quote pricing. Compare LearnWorlds (marketing-primary LMS) for course commerce, Connecteam for frontline training-lite hubs, and Breezy if hiring/ATS is the actual job.
editorialNotes: HR Wave-1 batch. Approved on hr-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=sop-training. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Trainual positions SOP templates, role charts, and training paths for operators who need process documentation without building a custom LMS. Score from first-party packaging, not lab testing.
Primary job is SOP knowledge base + employee training paths — strong sop-training cluster fit. Not scored as an ATS or time-clock peer.
Playbooks, subjects, tests, and completion tracking give solid training-path depth; e-sign and advanced governance land on higher tiers.
Slack/Google Workspace/Zapier-style support process distribution; not a full HRIS replacement.
Training content is consumable on mobile, but Trainual is not a deskless WFM/comms product — scored moderate for frontline readiness.
Completion and training reporting are marketed for managers; held at 7 vs deep L&D analytics suites.
FAQ best-fit 25–1000 employees plus Core→Enterprise ladder supports mid-market growth; micro teams may be underserved.
Opaque contact pricing plus a $1,000 implementation fee hurt transparency and entry value versus published ATS/WFM floors — capability is strong, price clarity is weak. Affiliate economics excluded.
AI-assisted documentation is published on higher tiers — useful for SOP drafting with plan gates rather than free unlimited AI.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the nine HR editorial criteria using the category weights (hiring/workforce fit 15, workflow depth 14, ease of use 12, integrations 12, value 12, mobile/frontline 10, scalability 9, analytics 8, AI 8), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — ATS/recruiting, frontline WFM, time & attendance, SOP training, and LMS peers are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
